episodes.192033: A favorable placement of the monsoon high over NM and then shifting to the west allowed for an influx of moisture and instability over the state of NM. Daily rounds of of showers and storms starting over the higher terrain midday spreading to lower elevation in the evening before slowly dissipating overnight each day. There were several reports of flash flooding over portions of central NM and a few severe thunderstorm wind gusts.
episodes.192204: The synoptic pattern largely remained ridge-dominant continuing on through mid July, but sufficient moisture helped trigger isolated diurnal convection which produced a small number of strong wind gusts across Utah.
episodes.192286: A cluster of thunderstorms produced a single severe hail report near the Washington/Lincoln county border on the evening of July 18th.
episodes.192287: An isolated severe thunderstorm developed around 1200MST in Phillips county, which then produced severe wind before exiting the county warning area. Additional severe thunderstorms developed across the plains during the evening hours, which produced a few severe wind gusts along with a large hail report near Limon.
episodes.192579: An area of strong to severe thunderstorms moved through portions of the Tucson Metro resulting in measured wind gusts in excess of 60 mph.
episodes.192611: A cold front approached from the west on the afternoon of July 18th. Out ahead of this front, isolated to widely scattered showers and thunderstorms developed and tracked eastwards across the Alligator River, Croatan and Roanoke Sounds, and coastal waters north of Oregon Inlet. Some of these storms became strong in nature producing damaging wind gusts.
episodes.192862: Nebraska was on the backside of an upper level trough with an upper ridge over most of the western half of the country. Temperatures were mostly in the 80s during the afternoon hours across south central Nebraska. Dewpoints were mostly in the 60s during the afternoon, and MUCAPE values were around 1000 to 2000 J/kg. Effective wind shear was generally around 35 to 45 knots. There was outflow from thunderstorms the previous night across northern Nebraska. Low-level lapse rates were generally 7 to 9 degrees C/km. DCAPE values were in excess of 1000 J/kg. These conditions resulted in storms with severe wind gusts to develop. ||Storms developed across northern and western Nebraska earlier in the day and moved southeastward. One of these storms moved into Furnas County and produced a couple of severe wind gusts between 3:30 PM and 4 PM CDT. Another storm moved in from the north and produced a severe wind gust in Webster County at 8:11 PM CDT.
episodes.193181: Scattered thunderstorms organized into a convective line with strong outflow winds across the southern Nebraska panhandle late in the afternoon and early in the evening on the 19th. Winds up to 70 mph were reported with these storms.
episodes.193198: SW steering over a moist and unstable airmass pushed the west coast sea breeze inland where it converged with the St. Johns River breeze and east coast sea breeze in the afternoon and evening.
episodes.193200: SW steering over a moist and unstable airmass pushed the west coast sea breeze inland where it converged with the St. Johns River breeze and east coast sea breeze in the afternoon and evening. These storms produced coastal wind gusts of 40-50 mph.
episodes.193467: A stationary front draped across the forecast area provided a focus for convection through the afternoon and evening hours. Flash flooding was favored with mean atmospheric flow parallel to the surface boundary and high precipitable water values. Isolated severe thunderstorms developed as well causing instances of wind damage where they occurred.
episodes.193477: A thunderstorm briefly became severe over far eastern Fall River County, producing strong wind gusts east of Oelrichs.
episodes.193478: A supercell thunderstorm developed over far southeast Harding and far southwest Perkins counties, then tracked south through Meade County. The storm produced large hail and very strong wind gusts before weakening as it moved near the Rapid City area.
episodes.193479: A strong thunderstorm produced hail to around penny size east of Rapid City.
episodes.193480: A thunderstorm briefly became severe in the Four Corners area, producing wind gusts to around 60 mph.
episodes.193755: A broken line of thunderstorms developed late morning across the central Sandhills. As this activity dropped south, portions of the line became severe over Frontier county where  wind gusts up to 60 MPH were reported. Later that afternoon, a supercell thunderstorm developed over southwestern Cherry county. This storm intensified and tracked south southwest during the evening hours, exiting southwestern Chase county after 9 PM CDT. This storm produced hail up to softball size and wind gusts approaching 80 MPH. Two individuals were injured from large hail in the Ogallala area. A center pivot irrigation system was overturned and the large hail led to total crop losses from Keith county south into western Chase county.
episodes.193936: During the late afternoon and early evening hours of the 19th a few discrete supercells developed over the south central Texas Panhandle that became severe dropping up to 1 hail along with gusts in excess of 58 mph. One of these cells moved SW into Deaf Smith County where it produced a wind gust of 75 mph measured by a mesonet near Bootleg.  Later into the evening a mesoscale convective system formed in SE CO and SW KS and moved south into the OK Panhandle where it produced some severe storms that created gusts up to 67 mph.
episodes.194172: Storms began to develop across northeast Colorado during the late morning hours of the 19th. Wind gusts up to 70 mph, along with wind damage to golf flags, were reported in northern Yuma county.
episodes.194173: Thunderstorms moved across Southwest Nebraska during the afternoon hours of the 19th which led to 50-60 mph winds in Dundy county, along with quarter size hail in Hitchcock county.
episodes.194279: Thunderstorms developed across portions of NW Kansas during the late morning through the afternoon hours. Hail up to golf ball size was reported in Logan county, along with 60-70 mph winds reported in Norton, Decatur, and Thomas counties.
episodes.194305: A high based thunderstorm collapsed near Worland and produced a 58 mph wind gust the Worland airport.
episodes.194478: Numerous thunderstorms developed in the late afternoon hours across Beaufort County. These thunderstorms produced frequent cloud to ground lightning, with several lightning strikes to homes and other structures.
episodes.194655: A couple thunderstorms embedded within a line along a cold front were able to become strong to severe east of I85. Microburst wind damage was able to bring down several trees.
episodes.194690: A thunderstorm passing through Bismarck during the early morning hours produced penny size hail.
episodes.194862: Scattered thunderstorms along a frontal boundary produced heavy rain which caused flash flooding across portions of northeast North Carolina.
episodes.194878: Thunderstorms developed across the eastern plains under a ridge of high pressure, bringing strong winds and hail to the far eastern plains.
episodes.194967: Monsoon moisture fueled isolated thunderstorms over the Mojave Desert. One storm produced flash flooding.
episodes.195048: A slow moving cluster of thunderstorms resided near Yankton for a couple hours, with a deep warm cloud layer resulting in extremely efficient rainfall rates of up to 3-4 inches per hour at times.  Rain totals from 3 to 6 inches were measured around the Yankton area over just a couple hours. Water quickly pooled and flowed up to a couple feet deep.
episodes.195070: Morning convection initiated over Lake Borgne during diurnal marine maximum. These storms were able to latch onto a boundary and produce a weak waterspout before dissipating shortly after.
episodes.195110: Monsoon moisture over northern Arizona produce showers and thunderstorms.  One storm produce heavy rain over the Verde Valley which flowed into the Verde River.
episodes.195131: Extensive damage from thunderstorms on July 19th.
episodes.195181: Isolated convection across northeast Nebraska brought an instance of flash flooding in Cedar County where a trained spotter reported water flowing over multiple county roads. There was also a funnel cloud the following day that received a lot of social media attention that developed over Norfolk. Additional funnels clouds were noted in Monona County the evening of the 21st.
episodes.195223: A weak shortwave in the flow around the dominant high pressure moved across eastern Utah and western Colorado on the 19th. This wave provided some enhanced instability and lift to the already modest instability and lift, as well as residual moisture, leading to a round of widespread showers and thunderstorms. However, with modest parameters and very dry surface layers, evidenced by inverted-V soundings, storms that did form were most favored to produce virga and strong, gusty winds.
episodes.195240: A thunderstorm wind gust exceeded 50 knots in Butte County.
episodes.195500: A complex of showers and strong thunderstorms moved east across northern Alabama from the early morning hours into the early afternoon hours. A few of these storms produced damaging winds.
